assessments.reasoning: The Resolution of names section expressly conditions UnboundLocalError on a reference to a local variable in the current function scope that has no value bound at use. Determine local classification from binding operations anywhere in the code block, then apply the exception rule at the actual point of use. A missing name has the broader NameError rule, and the documented subclass relationship is consistent with that rule. The exact input requires a read of a local in its current function scope. Class-block unbound handling, module names, and names redirected by global or nonlocal directives fall outside that condition. Adjacent sections give different lookup rules for the challenged categories, including global fallback for unbound class-block locals. None defeats the scoped function-local rule.

challenge.method: Compare the adjacent cases of a wholly missing name, an enclosing free variable, a global/nonlocal declaration, and class-body lookup against the cited function-local condition.
challenge.results: Adjacent sections give different lookup rules for the challenged categories, including global fallback for unbound class-block locals. None defeats the scoped function-local rule.

limitations: Missing names and names affected by global or nonlocal declarations follow their applicable resolution rules.
The text establishes the stated sufficient condition at the point of use. It does not enumerate every way a local can become unbound or establish behavior of a particular interpreter executable.
